activities.description: Writing 'How to analyse chemical (composition)' on the whiteboard.
Explaining the topic of analyzing the chemical composition of biomolecules.
Describing an experiment of crushing a piece of living material with trichloroacetic acid and filtering the solution through a cloth.
Drawing and explaining the separation of the solution into two parts: acid-soluble and acid-insoluble.
Labeling and explaining the acid-soluble particles as 'Bio micro molecules' and the acid-insoluble particles as 'Bio macro molecules,' specifically mentioning fatty acids as an example.

characterInteraction.description: The professor is the only character and interacts with the audience through his lecture.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The lecture presents a systematic approach to analyzing the chemical composition of biomolecules, focusing on practical experimentation and classification.

mood.description: Curious. The professor's clear explanation and the visual aid on the whiteboard contribute to a curious and engaged atmosphere.

narrativeProgression.description: The professor introduces a specific experiment to analyze biomolecules.
The experiment results in two types of solutions: acid-soluble and acid-insoluble.
The professor defines the acid-soluble and acid-insoluble particles as 'Bio micro molecules' and 'Bio macro molecules,' respectively.

scenes.thematicElements: Chemical composition of biomolecules. Classification of biomolecules into micro and macro molecules based on their solubility in acid.
scenes.title: Analyzing Biomolecules
